discipline: Every interaction in this concept was matched to an existing candidate family before an id was proposed. Statuses are reuse, alias, retire, supersede, preserve and candidate. Nothing here is canon; the exact names are adjudicated later against the real Command Catalog.
note_on_sameness: This adjudication is intentionally the same across concepts 05-11. The seven designs invoke the same semantic operations against the same canon; proposing seven different command sets would be invention, not a finding. What differs per concept is the ROUTE payload and the surface that raises the command, both recorded below.

concept_specific.navigate_payload: cmd.settings.navigate carries the destination object this concept parsed from the route, never a rendered index

raising_surfaces.home: search, one attention panel whose items carry inline fixes, then fewer and larger domain cards
raising_surfaces.navigation: a left rail plus a breadcrumb, with large cards as the main event at every width
raising_surfaces.manager: provider summary as high-value status cards followed by an explicit quick-actions row, then subpages
raising_surfaces.exact_result: the destination card or field is highlighted in place with a soft halo and a found-from-search caption

commands.note: Opening Settings is already a product command; the concepts are a surface for it, not a second entry point.
One command carrying the destination object, not one per level. The concepts' route grammar is its payload.
Payload must be the immutable result id and the resolved destination object. Routing by rendered position is the defect this pass exists to remove.
Candidate alias of cmd.settings.navigate with a domain destination; kept only if the catalog census finds existing callers.
Same: an alias of navigate with a page destination.
Focus and the locator highlight are one effect, not two commands.
The chip/bloom modal is the Settings contract these concepts supersede. Retire, keeping a compatibility alias to cmd.settings.navigate only if live callers exist.
The single hand-off used by all ten deferred named owners, carrying the owner name, the originating Settings destination and the return contract.
Returns to the surface that opened Settings, which is the origin the deep link recorded.
Needs expected-revision fencing: two windows editing one Project is the changed-elsewhere fixture.

There is no user-facing scope in a Project-only design. What survives is an inspector for WHY a value is what it is — candidate cmd.settings.value.explain — covering managed, unavailable, automatic and not-configured. Recorded as a rename, not a new capability.
Backs `Why this value?`. Read-only; returns origin, default, recommendation, restart requirement and availability reason.
Result must carry additions, replacements, unchanged, unavailable, conflicts and re-pointed account references as separate counts.
Atomic, restore-pointed, verified, receipted. No synchronisation follows it — there is deliberately no cmd.settings.link_projects.
The register has import.rollback but no copy rollback. The copy receipt is rollback-capable, so the candidate is needed or copy.apply must reuse the restore-point command.
Taken before any transaction. May resolve to an existing storage/backup owner command; flagged for census rather than assumed new.
Binds by installation identity, never by PATH order.
Explicit user-triggered first acquisition from the official source for the exact host. Auto/On is not consent.
Adopting a detected installation. Must refuse when ownership cannot be established — the unknown-owner fixture is manual-only.
Separate from installation, always.
Cached catalogue stays visible while refreshing; latest request wins.
Owned by Usage. Settings calls it and renders the answer; it never computes a balance.
Doctor has no command in the register and is a required family. Read-only projection plus named repairs; each repair is an existing owner command, not a new one.
Dispatches to the owning subsystem's repair command. Must never silently fix; it opens an ObservableWork operation.

every_action_needs: expected revision, idempotency, fencing and stale-result handling
GUI, natural-language, command-palette and automation equivalence
production wiring evidence and a regression fixture
